name: Disputes and partial refunds on the same ad
story: The $149 carousel took eight payments, but three are in open dispute and four had $120 refunded, so a gross $1,192 week is really a loss.

why.parent_carousel: 8 payments (excluded: 3 in open dispute) -> 5 counted orders, incl. 4 partly refunded, paid revenue $265.00; contribution = 265.00 x 0.70 - 265.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 5 = $175.13 vs spend $250 -> net -$74.87 (0.70 contribution per ad dollar). Disputed money is not settled and $120 of each partly refunded $149 went back, so only $265 of real revenue remains and the ad returns about 70 cents per ad dollar; three disputes plus four big refunds also say buyers feel misled. Cut it (reduce, or pause while the offer is fixed): the picture would change only if the disputes are later won, and unsettled money cannot justify spending now.
why.free_guide: 6 payments -> 6 counted orders, paid revenue $234.00; contribution = 234.00 x 0.70 - 234.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 6 = $153.86 vs spend $90 -> net +$63.86 (1.71 contribution per ad dollar). Six clean $39 orders return about $1.71 per ad dollar: increase is the natural move, keep is a reasonable judgement call.
why.holiday_static: 2 payments -> 2 counted orders, paid revenue $158.00; contribution = 158.00 x 0.70 - 158.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 2 = $104.90 vs spend $40 -> net +$64.90 (2.62 contribution per ad dollar). Two orders are too few to act on: keep.

name: Right at break-even
story: Two ads land within five cents of break-even per ad dollar after costs, one just above and one just below, while a third is clearly profitable.

why.trial_video: 5 payments -> 5 counted orders, paid revenue $245.00; contribution = 245.00 x 0.70 - 245.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 5 = $161.72 vs spend $160 -> net +$1.72 (1.01 contribution per ad dollar). One cent of profit per ad dollar is break-even within noise: keep is the plain answer and reduce is a defensible judgement call (extra spend usually buys slightly worse clicks); increase would push it into a loss and pause throws away a near break-even sales channel.
why.free_guide: 6 payments -> 6 counted orders, paid revenue $234.00; contribution = 234.00 x 0.70 - 234.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 6 = $153.86 vs spend $158 -> net -$4.14 (0.97 contribution per ad dollar). Losing three cents per ad dollar on six orders is break-even within noise: keep or reduce are both sensible judgement calls; increase is wrong and pause is an overreaction to a $4 gap.
why.parent_carousel: 4 payments -> 4 counted orders, paid revenue $396.00; contribution = 396.00 x 0.70 - 396.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 4 = $263.40 vs spend $90 -> net +$173.40 (2.93 contribution per ad dollar). Four clean $99 orders return about $2.93 per ad dollar: the money freed or held back from the break-even ads belongs here.

name: Four ads, three profitable at different strengths
story: Three of four ads make money after costs, one strongly, one moderately and one barely, while the holiday static loses money.

why.parent_carousel: 5 payments -> 5 counted orders, paid revenue $745.00; contribution = 745.00 x 0.70 - 745.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 5 = $496.77 vs spend $120 -> net +$376.77 (4.14 contribution per ad dollar). The strongest return by far on five clean orders: the first place for more money.
why.trial_video: 7 payments -> 7 counted orders, paid revenue $343.00; contribution = 343.00 x 0.70 - 343.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 7 = $226.41 vs spend $150 -> net +$76.41 (1.51 contribution per ad dollar). Solid profit on seven orders: increase or keep are both reasonable judgement calls.
why.free_guide: 8 payments -> 8 counted orders, paid revenue $232.00; contribution = 232.00 x 0.70 - 232.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 8 = $151.54 vs spend $135 -> net +$16.54 (1.12 contribution per ad dollar). Only 12 cents of profit per ad dollar, so keep is the sensible default; a small increase is defensible but riskier because extra spend can tip it under break-even. Never a cut while it is profitable.
why.holiday_static: 3 payments -> 3 counted orders, paid revenue $237.00; contribution = 237.00 x 0.70 - 237.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 3 = $157.34 vs spend $210 -> net -$52.66 (0.75 contribution per ad dollar). Returns about 75 cents per ad dollar on three orders: cut it and move the money to the carousel.

name: High-ticket ad with exactly three orders
story: The $199 holiday static has exactly three clean orders, just enough evidence to act on, while a $149 carousel with two orders is still too thin and the trial video loses money.

why.holiday_static: 3 payments -> 3 counted orders, paid revenue $597.00; contribution = 597.00 x 0.70 - 597.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 3 = $398.58 vs spend $240 -> net +$158.58 (1.66 contribution per ad dollar). Three orders meet the evidence bar and it returns about $1.66 per ad dollar: increase is justified, while keep is a fair judgement call because three big-ticket sales are lumpy. It must not be treated as too thin, and must not be cut.
why.parent_carousel: 2 payments -> 2 counted orders, paid revenue $298.00; contribution = 298.00 x 0.70 - 298.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 2 = $198.71 vs spend $100 -> net +$98.71 (1.99 contribution per ad dollar). Two $149 orders look profitable but are below the three-order bar: keep.
why.trial_video: 4 payments -> 4 counted orders, paid revenue $196.00; contribution = 196.00 x 0.70 - 196.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 4 = $129.38 vs spend $200 -> net -$70.62 (0.65 contribution per ad dollar). The most leads (26) but only about 65 cents back per ad dollar after costs: cut it.

name: Most leads is also the best after costs
story: The parent carousel brings the most leads and, unlike the usual trap, also the most profit after costs.

why.parent_carousel: 8 payments -> 8 counted orders, paid revenue $792.00; contribution = 792.00 x 0.70 - 792.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 8 = $526.80 vs spend $180 -> net +$346.80 (2.93 contribution per ad dollar). Most leads, eight clean orders and about $2.93 of contribution per ad dollar: here the lead leader really is the best ad, so increase it.
why.free_guide: 4 payments -> 4 counted orders, paid revenue $116.00; contribution = 116.00 x 0.70 - 116.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 4 = $75.77 vs spend $70 -> net +$5.77 (1.08 contribution per ad dollar). Profitable but thin margin (about eight cents per ad dollar) on four orders: keep is the sensible default, a small increase is a defensible judgement call; not a cut.
why.holiday_static: 1 payments -> 1 counted orders, paid revenue $199.00; contribution = 199.00 x 0.70 - 199.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 1 = $132.86 vs spend $90 -> net +$42.86 (1.48 contribution per ad dollar). One $199 sale is profitable on paper but is no evidence: keep.

name: Two losers, very different sizes
story: Two ads lose money after costs, one by about eight cents per ad dollar and one by about 74 cents, while the holiday static is clearly profitable.

why.parent_carousel: 3 payments -> 3 counted orders, paid revenue $297.00; contribution = 297.00 x 0.70 - 297.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 3 = $197.55 vs spend $215 -> net -$17.45 (0.92 contribution per ad dollar). A mild loss: reduce is the best move (it keeps a near break-even channel alive while costing less); pause is also acceptable. Not keep or increase.
why.free_guide: 3 payments -> 3 counted orders, paid revenue $87.00; contribution = 87.00 x 0.70 - 87.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 3 = $56.83 vs spend $220 -> net -$163.17 (0.26 contribution per ad dollar). Gets back about 26 cents per ad dollar, so every dollar loses about 74 cents: pause; trimming it would keep losing most of the budget.
why.holiday_static: 5 payments -> 5 counted orders, paid revenue $395.00; contribution = 395.00 x 0.70 - 395.00 x 0.0299 - 0.49 x 5 = $262.24 vs spend $100 -> net +$162.24 (2.62 contribution per ad dollar). Five clean $79 orders return about $2.62 per ad dollar: increase with the money taken from the losers; keep is a cautious alternative.
